title: AlphaFold Meets Flow Matching for Generating Protein Ensembles

nodes.text: AlphaFLOW and ESMFLOW repurpose pretrained single-state structure predictors (AlphaFold and ESMFold) as sequence-conditioned generative models of protein structure by fine-tuning them under a custom flow matching framework.
nodes.evidence: we repurpose highly accurate single-state predictors such as AlphaFold and ESMFold and fine-tune them under a custom flow matching framework to obtain sequence-conditoned generative models of protein structure called AlphaFLOW and ESMFLOW

nodes.text: Iterative denoising frameworks such as diffusion and flow matching provide a general recipe for converting regression models into generative models with little change to architecture and training objective.
nodes.evidence: iterative denoising frameworks (such as diffusion and flow-matching) provide a general recipe for converting regression models to generative models with relatively little modification to the architecture and training objective

nodes.text: Unlike inference-time MSA-ablation methods, the flow-matching strategy applies equally to protein-language-model-based predictors (e.g. ESMFold, OmegaFold) and can train or fine-tune on arbitrary ensembles such as molecular dynamics data, which MSA interventions cannot.
nodes.evidence: Unlike inference-time MSA ablation, this strategy applies equally well to PLM-based predictors and can be used to train or fine-tune on arbitrary ensembles

nodes.text: A structure-denoising architecture is built by prepending an input-embedding module similar to AlphaFold's template embedding stack to the pairwise folding trunks, making the denoiser a thin wrapper around well-validated single-structure predictors.
nodes.evidence: we develop an input embedding module very similar to AlphaFold's template embedding stack and prepend it to the pairwise folding trunks of AlphaFold and ESMFold... thin wrappers around well-validated single-structure predictors

nodes.text: The flow uses a harmonic (polymer-like) prior over beta-carbon coordinates with a linear interpolation conditional probability path (CondOT path), training via a squared FAPE loss in the SE(3)-quotient space toward the Frechet mean of the conditional distribution.
nodes.evidence: we define the prior distribution q(x) over the positions of these beta-carbons to be a harmonic prior... we aim to learn the more general Frechet mean of the conditional distribution

nodes.text: Flow matching improves over harmonic diffusion by imposing the prior as a boundary condition at t=0 for all dimensionalities (avoiding inference-time distributional shifts from training on small crops) and by handling missing/gap residues simply by omitting them in interpolation.
nodes.evidence: in flow matching, the prior distribution is imposed as a boundary condition at time t = 0 for all dimensionalities... flow matching provides an easy means to deal with missing (gap) residues... by simply omitting them in the interpolation

nodes.text: Score-matching in diffusion models can be viewed as a special case of flow matching, while flow matching circumvents certain difficulties that arise with diffusion.
nodes.evidence: Score-matching in diffusion models can be seen as a special case of flow matching; however... flow matching circumvents certain difficulties that would otherwise arise with diffusion

nodes.text: When trained on MD ensembles, the method belongs to the new generation of Boltzmann-targeting generative models that prioritize scalability and generalization over the exact likelihoods sought by earlier normalizing-flow Boltzmann generators which failed to scale beyond small molecules.
nodes.evidence: Our method, when trained on MD ensembles, can be viewed as belonging to this new generation of Boltzmann-targeting generative models

nodes.text: After fine-tuning only on PDB structures, AlphaFLOW/ESMFLOW substantially surpass the precision-diversity Pareto frontier of MSA-subsampling ablation baselines on a test set of recently deposited conformationally heterogeneous proteins.
nodes.evidence: we substantially surpass the precision-diversity Pareto frontier of MSA ablation baselines on a test set of recently deposited conformationally heterogeneous proteins

nodes.text: When further trained on the ATLAS molecular dynamics dataset and evaluated on structurally dissimilar test proteins, AlphaFLOW accurately captures conformational flexibility, atomic positional distributions, and higher-order ensemble observables such as intermittent contacts and solvent exposure.
nodes.evidence: AlphaFLOW substantially surpasses the MSA baselines in the prediction of conformational flexibility, distributional modeling of atomic positions, and replication of higher-order ensemble observables such as intermittent contacts and solvent exposure

nodes.text: When given a static PDB structure as a template, sampling from AlphaFLOW achieves faster wall-clock convergence to many equilibrium properties than running MD simulation from that structure, suggesting use as a proxy for expensive physics-based simulation.
nodes.evidence: sampling from AlphaFLOW provides faster wall-clock convergence to many equilibrium properties than running molecular dynamics (MD) simulation starting from that structure

nodes.text: The harmonic prior is improved over EigenFold's harmonic diffusion by defining a scale-invariant noising process resilient to missing and cropped residues.
nodes.evidence: improves over it by defining a scale-invariant noising process resilient to missing and cropped residues
